newsitem.title: USA: Compaq Q1 EPS in line but revs seen light.
newsitem.headline: Compaq Q1 EPS in line but revs seen light.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp's first quarter earnings were a bit better than Wall Street's consensus estimate, but analysts said revenues came in below some expectations.
Compaq reported first quarter earnings of $1.36 a share, versus $0.85 a year ago. The First Call consensus was $1.31.

"The bottom line number was very close to the First Call number, so no surprise there," said Bill Milton, a Brown Brothers Harriman analyst. "Although the company arrived at that number a bit differently than I had thought. There was a revenue shortfall here. The revenue line was disappointing."
Compaq said revenues grew 14.3 percent, to $4.8 billion from $4.2 billion a year ago.

"My estimate was $4.9 billion in revenues," said Daniel Ries, a Nomura Research analyst. "You can make the case that it was somewhat light." He said the shortfall appears to have come from the consumer business in North America.

However, Ries added, "It's a good solid quarter. The asset management is phenomenal. It's amazing the influence the new CFO has had on operations." Chief Financial Officer Earl Mason joined Compaq in May 1996.
Compaq executives began a conference call with analysts at 830 EDT/1230 GMT.
Compaq shares were down 1-1/8 at 73-5/8 in the first minutes of trading today.
"There is a common thread running through these technology company reports," Milton said. "Most of the bottom line numbers are in line with expectations, but the revenue has been disappointing."
Milton said Intel Corp's revenue guidance for the second quarter was disappointing, and revenues at Texas Instruments Inc were also a little light due to lower prices of memory chips.
